name: Lake Merced
note: Natural freshwater lake (a coastal lagoon fed by groundwater; an outlet to the ocean is on the 1869 Coast Survey map and was still mapped in 1881): present since before 1769 - year_start 1700 = 'always'. No c.1800 habitat layer covers it (SFEI Hidden Nature stops at 37.733 N), so the terrain treated it as a post-war pond (default 1945-65). Later causeways split it into South, North and East lakes.

name: Rodeo Lagoon
note: Natural coastal lagoon in a valley drowned by post-glacial sea-level rise ('mostly unaltered until the area was developed by the U.S. military'; the Army's 1937 road crossing cut off its east end): present since before 1769 - year_start 1700 = 'always'. No c.1800 habitat layer covers it, so the terrain treated it as a post-war pond (default 1945-65).

name: Abbotts Lagoon
note: Coastal lagoon behind a dune barrier on the Point Reyes peninsula, named for the Abbott brothers who leased the land in the mid-1800s (dairy ranches from 1857): natural, present since before 1769 - year_start 1700 = 'always'. No c.1800 habitat layer covers it, so the terrain treated it as a post-war pond (default 1945-65).

name: Lake Elizabeth (Fremont Central Park)
note: Shallow 83-acre man-made lake of Fremont Central Park (park development from 1960), dedicated in 1969 to the sister city Elizabeth, South Australia; 'much of the park was once the Stivers Lagoon'. Ring = today's water on ground the SFEI Alameda Creek layer maps as wet meadow / marsh c.1800; the cells it maps as the perennial pond of the old lagoon are left out, so the lagoon stays water before 1969. Year = dedication (the lake may have held water a few years earlier).

name: Shadow Cliffs Lake (Pleasanton)
note: Former Kaiser Industries gravel pit by the Arroyo del Valle, donated to the East Bay Regional Park District and 'opened as a park in 1971'. Year = park opening; the pit held water once quarrying below the water table stopped (late 1960s), not dated. On mapped c.1800 grassland, so without this row the terrain never showed it as water.

name: Quarry Lakes and the Niles gravel pits (Fremont)
note: Gravel pits of the Niles Sand and Gravel Co. along Alameda Creek (plant by 1912, expanded into today's park in 1954): 'by 1969 some of the gravel pits had been dug down to 120 feet below the surface, well below the water table' and the company pumped out the water the Alameda County Water District released for recharge until its pumping was declared an illegal waste of groundwater in 1976; the districts bought the land 1975-92 and opened the park 1997-2001. Year ESTIMATED = end of the pumping (the pits then filled); earlier ponds in worked-out pits are not dated. On mapped c.1800 grassland, so without this row the terrain never showed them as water.
